Same clause in Go Digit's Arogya Sanjeevani wording UIN GODHLIP24179V022324 (PDF dated Jan 2026). A formal repudiation also needs PMC/CRC approval (master circular para 17(a), HC-05). H018 'only means one thing' is a plain-words reading of this clause.

claim: On-screen tag at H009: NOT A CLAIM REJECTION [AROGYA SANJEEVANI POLICY WORDING]
source_quote: (v) The Company / TPA reserves the right to deny pre-authorization in case the insured person is unable to provide the relevant medical details. claim: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, ref IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024, dated 29 May 2024 (on-screen tags)
source_quote: Ref: IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/ 2024 Date: 29.05.2024 ... Sub: Master Circular on IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024- Health Insurance
note: irdai.gov.in original (English PDF 'Master Circular on Health Insurance Business -English.pdf' on this page; IRDAI's own health FAQ links this documentId). Its text is word-for-word identical to the basunivesh.com copy the writer used. Still current: IRDAI health FAQ page (dated 09 Oct 2026) cites it; no later health circular found in IRDAI's circular list to 22 Sep 2026.

claim: A TPA is a company registered with IRDAI that the insurer engages and pays a fee to handle cashless and claims; it sits between you and the insurer
source_quote: Third Party Administrator (TPA) means a company registered with the Authority, and engaged by an insurer, for a fee for providing health services such as cashless and claims administration, customer service to the policyholders. ... TPA act as intermediary between the insured and the insurer
note: IRDAI health FAQ (page dated 09 Oct 2026). The IRDAI (Third Party Administrators - Health Services) Regulations, 2016 are still in force (amended by the TPA (Amendment) Regulations, 2026, notified 31 Jul 2026), so the H015 tag stands.

claim: A TPA is a company licensed by IRDAI (H015)
source_quote: The launch of the much-awaited common third party administrator (TPA) floated by four state-owned general insurers has once again been postponed. ... The four general insurers have 23.75 per cent stake each and GIC Re has five per cent.
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per fact-check.md; Business Standard/PTI, 16 Aug 2015: Health Insurance TPA of India is owned by the four state-run general insurers and GIC Re. IRDAI's definition says only 'a company registered with the Authority'. Fix H015: 'A TPA is a company licensed by IRDAI.'

claim: IRDAI: TPA remuneration cannot depend on the claims paid out (Incurred Claim Ratio)
source_quote: In no case, the remuneration of TPAs shall depend upon the Incurred Claim Ratio (ICR) of the policies served by the TPAs;
note: Master circular Chapter II B.1; repeated in IRDAI health FAQ Q42 (Oct 2026). VO 'how much claim money gets paid out' is a fair plain-words gloss of ICR.

claim: No claim can be rejected without approval of the insurer's Claims Review Committee (or the PMC)
source_quote: No claim shall be repudiated without the approval of PMC or a three- member sub-group of PMC called the Claims Review Committee (CRC).
note: Para 17(a); repeated in the Policyholders' Interests master circular, 5 Sep 2024, Chapter on health claims 3(iii)4.

claim: A full or partial rejection must quote the specific policy terms
source_quote: In case, the claim is repudiated or disallowed partially, details shall be conveyed to the claimant along with full details giving reference to the specific terms and conditions of the policy document.
note: Para 17(b). On-screen tag [IRDAI MASTER CIRCULAR | PARA 17] is correct.

claim: Non-disclosure of a pre-existing disease, hospitalisation judged not medically necessary, and room-rent limits with proportionate deduction are common reasons for rejected or cut health claims
source_quote: Insurers have the right to deny claims and even cancel policies due to material non-disclosure. ... If a policyholder chooses a room beyond the allowed limit, they may face proportionate deductions, reducing the total reimbursement. ... Insurers only cover hospitalisation that is deemed medically necessary. If they determine that hospital admission was not required, the claim may be denied.
note: Business Today, 16 Feb 2025, relaying insurance advisor Nikhil Jha's list (it also lists PED and specific waiting periods, documents, diagnostic-only stays). Independent: CIO Annual Report 2023-24 p.77 health observations: 'Disclosing pre existing diseases or conditions, past ailments, treatment, will avoid rejection of claims under Mediclaim policies.'

claim: Before 60 months the insurer can still contest on non-disclosure; after 60 months of continuous cover it cannot, except for established fraud (on-screen clause quote at H036)
source_quote: No policy and claim of health insurance shall be contestable on any grounds of non-disclosure and/or misrepresentation except for established fraud, after the completion of the Moratorium Period, i.e. 60 months of continuous coverage
note: Para 13; the H036 on-screen quote matches word for word. Same rule in IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024, Schedule cl. 8, and IRDAI health FAQ Q39 (Oct 2026). '6 YEARS > 60 MONTHS' (H040) holds for continuous cover. Not covered by the VO: on an enhanced sum insured the 60 months run from the date of enhancement (see fact-check.md).

claim: Proportionate deduction: limit 5,000 vs room 8,000, so the insurer pays 5/8 (62.5%) of room-linked charges incl. surgery, doctor and nursing, a 37.5% cut; worked bill: cut about 60,000 vs a 9,000 room difference (OUR CALCULATION)
source_quote: In case of admission to a room/ICU/ICCU at rates exceeding the aforesaid limits, the reimbursement/payment of all other expenses incurred at the Hospital, with the exception of (a) cost of pharmacy and consumables, (b) cost of implants and medical devices, (c) cost of diagnostics, shall be effected in the same proportion as the admissible rate per day bears to the actual rate per day of Room Rent/ICU/ICCU charges.
note: Re-ran tools/claim_math.py: pays 62.5%, cuts 37.5%; cut 9,000 room + 45,000 surgeon/doctor + 5,625 nursing = 59,625 vs 9,000 room difference. Method matches this current wording (Go Digit Arogya Sanjeevani, UIN GODHLIP24179V022324). VO 'about thirty seven percent' = 37.5%. The claim_math.py docstring still credits the repealed 2020 guidelines (HC-09b).

claim: On-screen tag at H027 cites [AROGYA SANJEEVANI POLICY WORDING] for the proportionate deduction method
source_quote: In case of admission to a room/ICU/ICCU at rates exceeding the aforesaid limits, the reimbursement/payment of all other expenses incurred at the Hospital, with the exception of (a) cost of pharmacy and consumables, (b) cost of implants and medical devices, (c) cost of diagnostics, shall be effected in the same proportion as the admissible rate per day bears to the actual rate per day of Room Rent/ICU/ICCU charges.
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per fact-check.md; Annexure-6 of the 29.05.2024 master circular repeals item 2 'IRDAI/HLT/REG/CIR/194/07/2020 Consolidated Guidelines on Product Filing in Health Insurance Business' and item 19 'IRDAI/HLT/REG/CIR/151/06/2020 Modified Guidelines on Product filing in Health Insurance Business' (the proportionate-deduction norms). Change the tag to [AROGYA SANJEEVANI POLICY WORDING].

claim: Many policies do not apply the proportionate cut to medicines, and some also leave out implants and tests; check your policy wording (H028)
source_quote: In case of admission to a room/ICU/ICCU at rates exceeding the aforesaid limits, the reimbursement/payment of all other expenses incurred at the Hospital, with the exception of (a) cost of pharmacy and consumables, (b) cost of implants and medical devices, (c) cost of diagnostics, shall be effected in the same proportion as the admissible rate per day bears to the actual rate per day of Room Rent/ICU/ICCU charges.
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per fact-check.md; True only of the 11 Jun 2020 circular IRDAI/HLT/REG/CIR/151/06/2020, which the 29 May 2024 master circular repealed (Annexure-6 item 19). No replacement in the 2024 health master circular, the Insurance Products Regulations 2024, or the Policyholders' Interests master circular (it only says a policy must state 'The sub-limits, Proportionate Deductions and the existence of Package rates if any'). Current wordings differ: Go Digit Arogya Sanjeevani (2026) exempts pharmacy and consumables, implants and devices, diagnostics but applies the ratio when ICU exceeds its cap; IFFCO-Tokio Arogya Sanjeevani (2024) and the New India Mediclaim CIS exempt only medicines. Outlook Money (29 Sep 2026) credits the four exemptions to the 2024 circular, but its text has no such clause. Rewrite H028 (fact-check.md). Corrected claim sourced to current wordings: Go Digit Arogya Sanjeevani exempts pharmacy/consumables, implants, diagnostics; IFFCO-Tokio Arogya Sanjeevani and New India Mediclaim exempt only medicines. ICU dropped from VO and picture.

claim: The moratorium period used to be eight years (96 months); it is now 60 months (five years)
source_quote: After completion of eight continuous years under the policy no look back to be applied. This period of eight years is called as moratorium period.
note: IRDAI Guidelines on Standardization of General Terms and Clauses in Health Insurance Policy Contracts, IRDAI/HLT/REG/CIR/152/06/2020, 11 Jun 2020, clause 12 (repealed in 2024, so it shows the old rule). 60 months: master circular para 13 and Insurance Products Regulations 2024 Schedule cl. 8. '60 MONTHS · NO BREAK' matches '60 months of continuous coverage'.

claim: In 2024 IRDAI brought the moratorium down from eight to five years [IRDAI INSURANCE PRODUCTS REGULATIONS | 2024] (H033)
source_quote: Hyderabad, the 20th March, 2024 ... (2) These regulations shall come into force from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette or 1st April, 2024, whichever is later. ... After completion of sixty continuous months of coverage (including portability and migration) in health insurance policy, no policy and claim shall be contestable by the insurer on grounds of non-disclosure, misrepresentation, except on grounds of established fraud.
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per fact-check.md; The five-year rule is in the IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024 (gazette 22 Mar 2024, in force 1 Apr 2024); the 29 May 2024 master circular restated it and gave insurers until 30.09.2024 to change existing products. Fix: 'In twenty twenty four, IRDAI brought it down from eight years to five years.' Tag: [IRDAI INSURANCE PRODUCTS REGULATIONS | 2024].

claim: Porting or migrating keeps your moratorium years; cancelling and buying a new policy starts the count again
source_quote: Note :The accrued credits gained under the ported and migrated policies shall be counted for the purpose of calculating the Moratorium period.
note: Para 13 note; para 12(d) carries the moratorium credit on porting. Restart: the rule needs '60 months of continuous coverage'; IRDAI health FAQ Q33 on a break in policy: 'Accrued benefits may be lost completely.'

claim: The moratorium does not remove normal policy limits and exclusions
source_quote: After the expiry of Moratorium Period no health insurance policy shall be contestable except for proven fraud and permanent exclusions specified in the policy contract.
note: Customer Information Sheet format, Annexure-1 to the 29.05.2024 master circular (same irdai.gov.in page). Limits: Go Digit Arogya Sanjeevani wording (2026): 'The policies would however be subject to all limits, sub limits, co-payments, deductibles as per the policy contract.'

claim: The insurer must decide a cashless request within one hour
source_quote: Insurer shall decide on the request for cashless authorization immediately but not more than one hour of receipt of request.
note: Para 15(b). Unchanged as of Oct 2026: repeated in the Policyholders' Interests master circular (5 Sep 2024) and IRDAI health FAQ Q24/Q40 (page dated 09 Oct 2026); no later circular found.

claim: Final discharge approval within three hours; the patient must not be made to wait; any extra hospital charge for the delay is paid by the insurer from shareholders' funds
source_quote: Insurer shall grant final authorization within three hours of the receipt of discharge authorization request from the hospital. In no case, the policyholder shall be made to wait to be discharged from the Hospital. ... If there is any delay beyond three hours, the additional amount if any charged by the hospital shall be borne by the insurer from shareholder’s fund.
note: Para 16(a),(b); tags [PARAS 15–16] and [PARA 16(b)] correct. Unchanged as of Oct 2026 (Policyholders' Interests master circular 2024; IRDAI health FAQ Oct 2026).

claim: File reimbursement within the policy's time limit: some policies give fifteen days from discharge, some thirty (H051, on-screen 15–30 DAYS)
source_quote: Reimbursement of hospitalization, day care and ... prehospitalization expenses ... Within Fifteen days of date of discharge from ... hospital
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per fact-check.md; Limits differ between current standard-product wordings: Go Digit Arogya Sanjeevani (2026) gives 15 days; IFFCO-Tokio Arogya Sanjeevani (2024) gives 'Within thirty days of date of discharge from hospital'. 'Usually thirty' could make a viewer miss a 15-day limit. Fix H051 and its on-screen text (fact-check.md). IFFCO-Tokio Arogya Sanjeevani (2024): 'Within thirty days of date of discharge from hospital'.

claim: Complain to the insurer's grievance officer; the insurer must resolve or reply within 14 days
source_quote: On receipt of a complaint, the complainant will have to be given an acknowledgement immediately. Insurers should provide resolution to the complaint within 14 days along with the reasons for not accepting the complaint with specific reference to the relevant terms and conditions of the policy.
note: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024, 5 Sep 2024; the H053 tag is correct. Still 14 days in IRDAI health FAQ Q40 (Oct 2026) and on the Bima Bharosa home page ('Your complaint will be attended to within 14 days'); Bima Bharosa's older FAQ still says 15 days. Grievance officer: Bima Bharosa FAQ 'Approach the Grievance Redressal Officer of its branch or any other office that you deal with.'

claim: Bima Bharosa (bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in) is IRDAI's complaint portal; a complaint goes to the insurer and IRDAI can see and track it
source_quote: A complaint registered through Bima Bharosa will flow to the insurer's system as well as the IRDAI repository.
note: Policyholders' Interests master circular 2024: 'register the complaint on-line at IRDAI’s Bima Bharosa by visiting https://bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in/' and insurers must mirror their grievance data to Bima Bharosa in real time. URL on screen is correct.

claim: You can go to the Ombudsman if the insurer rejects your complaint or does not reply within 30 days (one month)
source_quote: Insurance Company/Insurance Broker has failed to furnish reply to you within a period of one month of your complaint; ... you can escalate the complaint to us if it's unresolved after 30 days.
note: Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017, Rule 14(3)(a): rejected, no reply within one month, or not satisfied with the reply.

claim: The Ombudsman website is cioins.co.in and complaints can be filed online
source_quote: The complaint can be made by the insured himself or by his legal heirs, nominee or assignee either through a written complaint duly signed by him or through electronic mail or online through the online platform developed by the Council of Insurance Ombudsmen through the website
note: CIO FAQ Q6 (the site named is www.cioins.co.in); Rule 14(2) as amended in 2021 allows online complaints.

claim: The Ombudsman system was set up by the government
source_quote: The Institution of Insurance Ombudsman was created by the Government of India under the Redressal of Public Grievances Rules, 1998, (RPG Rules) notified in official gazette, on 11th Nov. 1998. The RPG rules have been replaced by Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017, vide Gazette notification 413 (E) dated 25.04.2017
note: CIO Annual Report 2024-25, Introduction, printed p.1 (scanned; read from the page image). The Rules open: 'the Central Government hereby makes the following rules'. The [INSURANCE OMBUDSMAN RULES, 2017] tag is correct.

claim: The Ombudsman system was set up by the government to settle complaints of policyholders against insurance companies (H059, 'only' dropped)
source_quote: 2. The objects of these Rules is to resolve all complaints of all personal lines of insurance, group insurance policies, policies issued to sole proprietorship and micro enterprises on the part of insurance companies and their agents and intermediaries in a cost effective and impartial manner.
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per fact-check.md; The Ombudsman also hears complaints against agents, intermediaries and insurance brokers (Rule 13(1), 14(1)). Fix: drop 'only' (fact-check.md).

claim: Filing an Ombudsman complaint is free
source_quote: Insurance Ombudsman/CIO does not charge any fees for grievance redressal.
note: CIO FAQ Q15: 'No charges are required to be paid for lodging a complaint with the Insurance Ombudsman.'

claim: You can present your case yourself, without a lawyer
source_quote: Do I need to approach the Insurance Ombudsman through a lawyer? Our Response : As per the Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017, there is no provision to engage a lawyer.
note: CIO FAQ Q12. Rule 14(1): a person 'may himself or through his legal heirs, nominee or assignee, make a complaint'. The [CIOINS.CO.IN] tag on 'FREE · NO LAWYER NEEDED' is correct.

claim: File the Ombudsman complaint within one year of the insurer's final reply
source_quote: Complaint can lodged with the Office of the Insurance Ombudsman within one year from a) date of rejection of the complaint by the Insurance Company/Insurance Broker OR (b) expiry of one month of filing the complaint if the Insurer fails to reply
note: CIO FAQ Q8 (source typo 'can lodged' kept); Rule 14(3)(b). The VO leaves out the 'one month with no reply' trigger, which is acceptable.

claim: Ombudsman offices received 32,503 health insurance complaints in FY 2024-25 (VO: over thirty two thousand)
source_quote: OFFICE OF THE COUNCIL FOR INSURANCE OMBUDSMEN Complaints Disposal Statement for the period 01.04.2024 to 31.03.2025 STATEMENT H3 HEALTH INSURANCE ... Received during the period ... Total 4928 32503 37431
note: CIO Annual Report 2024-25, Statement H3 Health Insurance (scanned; headers on printed p.46 = PDF p.55, totals row on printed p.47 = PDF p.56; read from the page images): O/s at beginning 4928, received 32503, total 37431, recommendations 9417, awards fvg complainant 6126, awards fvg ins.co. 4897, withdrawal 3649, non-entertainable 4928, total disposed 29017; disposed within 3 months 22791, 3 months to 1 year 4343, above 1 year 1883; outstanding 8414. Totals checked: 4928+32503 = 37431; 9417+6126+4897+3649+4928 = 29017; 22791+4343+1883 = 29017; 37431-29017 = 8414. 2024-25 is the latest report (no 2025-26 report on cioins.co.in).

claim: About 3 in 4 (76%) of health complaints the Ombudsman settled (mediation) or decided by award went in the policyholder's favour, FY 2024-25 (OUR CALCULATION)
source_quote: RECOMMENDATIONS AND AWARDS IN FAVOUR OF COMPLAINANTS (COMPANYWISE) FOR THE PERIOD FROM 01.04.2024 TO 31.03.2025 STATEMENT H5 HEALTH INSURANCE ... Total 9423 8769.72 6126 6356.96 15543 15126.68
note: Re-ran tools/claim_math.py: (9417 recommendations + 6126 awards for complainant) / (9417 + 6126 + 4897 awards for insurer) = 15543/20440 = 76.0%. Fair method: the CIO itself counts recommendations plus awards as 'in favour of complainants' (Statement H5, printed p.55, same total 15543), and under Rule 16 a recommendation is a mediated settlement the complainant accepts 'as full and final'. H5 lists 9423 recommendations against 9417 in H3, a 6-case mismatch in the report; 76% either way. For the description: as a share of all 29,017 disposed complaints (incl. withdrawn and non-entertainable) it is 53.6%. CIO Annual Report 2024-25, Statement H3 Health Insurance (scanned; headers on printed p.46 = PDF p.55, totals row on printed p.47 = PDF p.56; read from the page images): O/s at beginning 4928, received 32503, total 37431, recommendations 9417, awards fvg complainant 6126, awards fvg ins.co. 4897, withdrawal 3649, non-entertainable 4928, total disposed 29017; disposed within 3 months 22791, 3 months to 1 year 4343, above 1 year 1883; outstanding 8414.

claim: About 8 in 10 (78.5%) health complaints were closed within three months, FY 2024-25 (OUR CALCULATION)
source_quote: Durationwise disposal of Complaints ... Within 3 months ... 3 months to 1 year ... Above 1 year ... Total Disposed ... 22791 4343 1883 29017
note: 22791/29017 = 78.5% (claim_math.py). CIO measures this from the date of registration (2023-24 report: 'within 90 days from the date of registration'). Includes complaints closed as non-entertainable, so the VO's 'closed' is the right word. CIO Annual Report 2024-25, Statement H3 Health Insurance (scanned; headers on printed p.46 = PDF p.55, totals row on printed p.47 = PDF p.56; read from the page images): O/s at beginning 4928, received 32503, total 37431, recommendations 9417, awards fvg complainant 6126, awards fvg ins.co. 4897, withdrawal 3649, non-entertainable 4928, total disposed 29017; disposed within 3 months 22791, 3 months to 1 year 4343, above 1 year 1883; outstanding 8414.

claim: The Ombudsman can award up to fifty lakh rupees
source_quote: (ii) not award compensation exceeding rupees 3 [fifty] lakhs (including relevant expenses, if any).
note: Rule 17(3) proviso (ii); '3 [fifty]' is the footnote showing Insurance Ombudsman (Amendment) Rules 2023, G.S.R. 828(E), 9 Nov 2023, which replaced 'thirty' with 'fifty'. No later amendment on cioins.co.in (rules page 'as amended till 09.11.2023'; latest CIO notification 29.07.2026).

claim: On-screen at H064: ₹50 LAKH [OMBUDSMAN RULES | RULE 17] · 30 DAYS · ₹5,000/DAY [IRDAI POLICYHOLDERS' INTERESTS MASTER CIRCULAR | 2024]
source_quote: The Insurer is required to comply with the award of the Insurance Ombudsman within 30 days of receipt of award by the Insurer. In case the Insurer does not honour the ombudsman award, a penalty of Rs. 5000/- per day shall be payable to the complainant.
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per fact-check.md; Para 20 covers 30 days and ₹5,000/day only; the ₹50 lakh cap is in Ombudsman Rules 17(3) (HC-28). Split the tag (fact-check.md).

claim: The award is binding on the insurer; it must comply within 30 days, else a ₹5,000-a-day penalty is payable to the complainant
source_quote: The Insurer is required to comply with the award of the Insurance Ombudsman within 30 days of receipt of award. ... In case the Insurer does not honour the Insurance Ombudsman award within 30 days, a penalty of Rs. 5000/- per day shall be payable to the complainant for each day of delay.
note: Binding: Ombudsman Rules 17(8) 'The award of Insurance Ombudsman shall be binding on the insurers'; Rule 17(6) 30 days. Also master circular para 20 and IRDAI health FAQ Q45 (Oct 2026). Penalty unchanged through Oct 2026, but see HC-29b.

claim: Unless the company challenges the award, it must pay within thirty days or pay a ₹5,000-a-day penalty to the complainant (H064)
source_quote: This provision will not be applicable in case insurer chooses to appeal against the award of the Insurance Ombudsman within 30days. In such case, due intimation shall be sent to the Policyholder.
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per fact-check.md; Policyholders' Interests master circular 2024, Implementation of Ombudsman Award (iv). Add 'Unless the company challenges the award' (fact-check.md).

claim: If you are not happy with the award, you can still go to a consumer court
source_quote: The award of Insurance Ombudsman shall be binding on the insurers (or insurance broker, as the case may be). However, if the complainant is not satisfied with the decision of the Insurance Ombudsman, he/she may exercise the right to take recourse to the normal process of law against the Insurance Company/Insurance Broker.
note: CIO FAQ Q21. A consumer commission is one route under 'the normal process of law'; the IRDAI citizen's charter (Policyholders' Interests master circular 2024) also lists 'Insurance Ombudsman / Consumer Court' as options. Order matters the other way: no Ombudsman complaint if the same matter is already before a court or consumer forum (Rule 14(5)).

claim: If you declare a condition the insurer may add a waiting period or charge a loading, but a declared condition cannot later be called non-disclosure
source_quote: Waiting period for pre-existing diseases disclosed by the persons to be insured, shall be maximum up to 36 months of continuous coverage under the Health Insurance policy.
note: Insurance Products Regulations 2024 Schedule cl. 7. Loading: the master circular's product-filing form (Annexure-3, 4.3) asks 'Whether any loading based on the health status are applicable'. Disclosure protects: IRDAI health FAQ Q4 'Concealing facts can lead to disputes when making a claim and the Insurer may reject the claim and even cancel the policy'; CIO 2023-24: disclosing PED 'will avoid rejection of claims'.

claim: Some policies cap room rent at 1% of the sum insured per day; these capped policies cost less, and going over the cap triggers the proportionate cut
source_quote: Room Rent, boarding and nursing expenses as provided by the Hospital not exceeding 1.0 % of the ... Sum Insured (without Cumulative Bonus) per day. ... On payment of additional premium, proportionate deduction clause shall stand deleted.
note: New India Mediclaim Policy CIS, UIN NIAHLIP23187V052223 (Mar 2023). Second insurer: SBI General Health Insurance Policy - Retail prospectus 'Room, Board & Nursing Expenses & Service Charges Etc - Up to 1% of the SI per day.' (2021). One night over the cap can cut surgery charges because the ratio applies to 'all other expenses incurred at the Hospital' (HC-09); how much depends on the wording.

claim: Gloves, masks, syringes and similar items are often not paid by a normal policy
source_quote: MASK (Not Payable) ... List V – Additional Non Payable Items ... Band Aids, Bandages, Sterile Injections, Needles, Syringes ... Examination Gloves
note: Go Digit Arogya Sanjeevani wording (2026), Annexure A non-payable lists (sterilised gloves are payable, unsterilised gloves are not). IFFCO-Tokio's 2024 wording lists GLOVES and MASK under 'Items for which coverage is not available in the policy'.

claim: Reports say consumables can be five to fifteen percent of a hospital bill (H075, on-screen AS REPORTED [OUTLOOK MONEY | BUSINESS STANDARD])
source_quote: So, you may have to pay 10-15 per cent of your hospital bill from your own pocket.
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per fact-check.md; Outlook Money, 22 Jan 2026. Other figures: Business Standard 10 Jul 2021 'According to industry estimates, consumables earlier made up between 2 per cent and 8 per cent of hospital bills. But during the pandemic, this has increased to 15-20 per cent'; Max Bupa (same article) 'earlier 5-10 per cent of the bill was consumable items'; Bajaj Allianz (same) 'approximately 8-10 per cent of the hospital bill before the pandemic'. The VO must attribute ('Reports say'), retag on screen, and put the range of figures in the description (fact-check.md).

claim: Some insurers sell an add-on cover for consumables (H075)
source_quote: Some health insurance products provide consumables coverage as an optional feature.
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per fact-check.md; Sources say 'some' (Outlook Money 2026; Business Standard 2021 'Some insurance companies have come up with riders'). Fix: 'Some insurers sell an add on cover for this.'

claim: Claim denials and cuts happen to many families in India
source_quote: During 2024-25, insurers have settled about 87 per cent of total number of claims registered in their books and have repudiated about 8 per cent of them and the remaining about 5 per cent were pending for settlement as on 31st March 2025.
note: IRDAI Annual Report 2024-25, I.6.5.6; Table I.29: 29.51 lakh health claims repudiated and ₹18,521 crore disallowed in 2024-25. Survey: Business Today, 2 Jan 2025, LocalCircles 'over 50% of health insurance policyholders who submitted claims in the last three years experienced either rejection or partial approval' (self-selected online survey). 'Middle class' is framing, not measured.

claim: Usually the papers go to a TPA, not the insurer's own staff
source_quote: In terms of number of claims settled, 69 per cent of the claims were settled through TPAs and the balance 31 per cent of the claims were settled through in-house mechanism.
note: IRDAI Annual Report 2024-25, I.6.5.5. FY 2023-24: 72 per cent through TPAs (Business Standard, 30 Dec 2024, citing the IRDAI annual report).

claim: The only exception is fraud: not a small mistake or a forgotten fever, and it has to be established
source_quote: For the purpose of this clause, the expression "fraud" means any of the following acts committed by the Insured Person or by his agent or the hospital/doctor/any other party acting on behalf of the insured person, with intent to deceive the insurer or to induce the insurer to issue an insurance Policy ... The company shall not repudiate the claim and/or forfeit the policy benefits on the ground of fraud, if the insured person / beneficiary can prove that the misstatement was true to the best of his knowledge and there was no deliberate intention to suppress the fact
note: 'Established fraud' is from master circular para 13; the fraud definition (intent to deceive) and the honest-misstatement defence are from the current standard wording (Go Digit 2026; same text in the repealed 2020 IRDAI general-terms guidelines). 'Fraud that the company has to establish' is a fair plain-words reading; optional tighter wording is in fact-check.md.
